rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan without disagreement and is commonly placed eleventh in revelation order, after al-Fajr.
rows.anchor: السورة مكية بلا خلاف، والمشهور أنها الحادية عشرة في ترتيب النزول. نزلت بعد الفجر

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators agree that the occasion was the early delay of revelation, which distressed the Prophet.
rows.anchor: المفسرون مجمعون على أن سبب النزول، هو إبطاء الوحي في أوائله على الرسول

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: One report says the Prophet told Khadija that his Lord had forsaken and hated him; she reassured him and the verse came down.
rows.anchor: ففي رواية أنه رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وقد شكا إلى زوجة السيدة خديجة

rows.speaker: السيدة خديجة
rows.claim: A second report makes Khadija the speaker who was troubled by the pause in revelation.
rows.anchor: وفي راوية ثانية، أنها السيدة خديجة، وقد رابها فتور الوحي

rows.speaker: أم جميلة امرأة أبي لهب
rows.claim: A third report says Umm Jamil taunted Muhammad that his demon had abandoned him.
rows.anchor: هي التي قالت: يا محمد! ما أرى شيطانك إلا قد تركك

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: A fourth report says the polytheists gloated that Muhammad's Lord had abandoned and hated him.
rows.anchor: ورواية رابعة تقول: إن المشركين هم الذين قالوا في شماتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports of occasions are contextual clues, not necessarily causal legal explanations; early authorities admit uncertainty and disagreement, and the verses came down around the event.
rows.anchor: أسباب النزول لا تعدو أ، تكون قرائن مما حول النص، وهي بإعتراف الأقدمين أنفسهم لا تخلو من وهم

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: The prevailing earlier view treats Qur'anic oaths as glorifying what is sworn by, since created things are great signs.
rows.anchor: الرأي السائد عند الأقدمين، أن هذا القسم القرآني يحمل معنى التعظيم للمقسم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the night oath as glorification can require strained interpretations because night can also evoke loneliness, death, graves, and estrangement.
rows.anchor: لحظوا فيه كذلك - في آية الضحى - معنى الاستيحاش، وأنه وقت الغم

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh explains the duha oath as drawing attention to the light's greatness and its status as a major sign and blessing.
rows.anchor: فالقسم بالضياء للإشارة إلى تعظيم أمر الضياء وإعظام قدر النعمة فيه

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh likens night to divine majesty through its fearful stilling power, while also noting its benefits for bodily and mental rest.
rows.anchor: فهذا سلطان من الخوف مبهم، لا تحيط بأسبابه ولا بتفصيل أطواره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds this search for grandeur in night forced by an assumed rule that every oath must glorify its object.
rows.anchor: اضطر - تحت سيطرة فكرة التعظيم بالقسم - إلى التماس وجه الإعظام فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier interpreters explain night in general, although the verse specifically qualifies it as the night when it settles.
rows.anchor: التمسوا العظمة في الليل، مطلق الليل. مع أنه مقيد في الآية بـ {إِذَا سَجَى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues that interpreters conflate glorification with the wisdom of creation; every created thing has wisdom, which alone does not establish an oath's intended grandeur.
rows.anchor: خلطوا بين الإعظام، والحكمة في خلق المقسم به، وما من شيء من مخلوقات الله لم يخلق لحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's wāw can serve a rhetorical purpose beyond glorification: strongly directing attention to familiar sensory realities that prepare the reader for unseen meanings.
rows.anchor: القسم بها يمكن أن يكون، والله أعلم، قد خرج عن أصل الوضع اللغوي في القسم للتعظيم، إلى معنى بياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quality selected for the oath suits its context; any impression of glorification strengthens the attention rather than defining the device's main purpose.
rows.anchor: واختيار المقسم به تراعى فيه الصفة التي تناسب الموقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daily alternation from bright duha to a quiet night is a sensory image that prepares for the unseen pause in revelation, without suggesting that heaven abandoned earth.
rows.anchor: تألق الضوء في ضحوة النهار، ثم فتور الليل إذا سجا وسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sensory contrast between light and darkness can clarify unseen guidance and truth or misguidance and falsehood.
rows.anchor: معاني من الهدى والحق، أو الضلال والباطل، بماديات من النور والظلمة

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي ونظام الدين النيسابوري
rows.claim: They compare alternating night and day, which wax and wane by wisdom, to revelation being sent and withheld according to divine purposes.
rows.anchor: فمرة تزداد ساعات الليل وتنقص ساعات النهار، ومرة بالعكس، فلا تكون الزيادة لهوى

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي ونظام الدين النيسابوري
rows.claim: They also say the oath answers the disbelievers' taunt: they were unable to prove their claim that God had abandoned Muhammad.
rows.anchor: هاتوا الحجة، فعجزوا، فلزمه اليمين بأنه ما ودعه ربه ما قلاه

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي ونظام الدين النيسابوري
rows.claim: A further interpretation compares night and day alternately prevailing to how no created people are exempt from such change.
rows.anchor: أنظر إلى جوار الليل مع النهار، لا يسلم أحدهما عن الآخر

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh says the Prophet's distress during the pause was relieved by renewed revelation: duha represents life-giving first revelation, while quiet night restores strength for later work.
rows.anchor: فآتاه الله ما كان في شوق إليه، وثبته بالوحي وبشره أن تلك الفترة لم تكن عن ترك ولا عن قلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's sensory analogy is nearly lost in Abduh's account of night as rest and preparation for work.
rows.anchor: ويوشك الملحظ البيلني، أن يتوه وسط هذا الكلام في الضحى تقوى به الحياة

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim comes close to matching the bright duha after darkness with revelation after its pause, but frames the oath as proof of God's lordship, wisdom, and mercy.
rows.anchor: وكان "إبن قيم الجوزية" أقرب إلى إدراك الملحظ البياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Ibn al-Qayyim's appeal to doubts about God's lordship misses the stated occasion, which concerns a claim that God abandoned Muhammad.
rows.anchor: الموقف كان ارتياباً من المشركين في ربوبية الله وحكمته ورحمته، وإنما كان - على قول المفسرين في سبب النزول - كلاماً

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some interpret the order of duha then night as preferring life until believers reach maturity, avoiding despair first and then fear of divine plotting.
rows.anchor: إنه إشارة أن الحياة أولى للمؤمن من الموت إلى أن تحصل كمالاته الممكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds no clear connection between the oath and its answer in the accounts of al-Tabari, al-Zamakhshari, and Abu Hayyan, and notes they do not compare it with God's explicit denials of oaths.
rows.anchor: لم يتعرض "إبن جرير الطبري" لبيان ارتباط المقسم به

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports disagreements over whether duha means the whole day or one daytime hour, and whether saja means night arriving, departing, settling, or becoming still.
rows.anchor: فهم النهار كله، وهو ساعة من ساعات النهار

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari selects daylight, understood as visible sunlight, for duha and stillness among its people for saja.
rows.anchor: واختار "الطبري" من هذه الأقوال في الضحى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari defines duha as the early day when the sun rises and shines, while also reporting that it can mean the whole day; saja is settled darkness or quiet people and sounds.
rows.anchor: هو صدر النهار حين ترتفع الشمس وتلقى شعاعها، وقيل: أريد بالضحى النهار

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says saja may mean night departing or arriving.
rows.anchor: عند أبي حيان: سجا الليل أدبر، وقيا: أقبل

rows.speaker: الفراء وابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Al-Farra says saja means that night darkened and rested, while Ibn al-A'rabi says its darkness intensified.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: أظلم ورك، وقال إب الأعرابي: أشتد ظلامه

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi allows saja to mean that people become still, a figurative attribution to night.
rows.anchor: أن يكون معنى سجا، سكن الناس فيه، فيكون الإسناد مجازياً

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh defines duha as sunlight in the day's prime and saja as the quiet and inactivity of night-time inhabitants.
rows.anchor: هو ضوء الشمس في شباب النهار. وفي سجا الليل: هو ما تجده من سكون أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the words can carry several lexical senses, the rhetoric of this particular setting admits only the single sense that best fits it.
rows.anchor: البلاغة لا تجيز إلا معنى واحداً في المقام الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sensory uses of the duha root center on visibility and exposure; most commonly, duha names the defined early daytime when the sun's light becomes clear, and it can name an act at that time.
rows.anchor: ودلالة الوضوح هي الملحوظة في كل الإستعمالات الحسية للمادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic uses include duha opposite evening, the sun's light brought forth, and a specific time appointed for events; these usages weigh against interpreting it as the whole day.
rows.anchor: وفي الاستعمال القرآني، نرى القرآن الكريم استعمل الضحى مقابلاً للعشية

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub explains that the sacrificial day is called adha from the sheep sacrificed at duha.
rows.anchor: وقال "يعقوب" في الأضحى: يسمى اليوم أضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointment of people at duha in 20:59 and its use opposite evening in 79:46 show that duha means a specific daytime period, not the whole day; the same reading fits the sun's duha in 91:1.
rows.anchor: مما يبعد تفسير الضحى بأنه النهار كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saja means the lull or stillness of night, not its arrival or departure; its contrast with duha and Arabic uses of the root support this sense.
rows.anchor: فالسكون أو الفتور هو ما يلائم الموقف بيانياً، وليس الإقبال ولا الإدبار

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says duha was chosen because it was when God spoke to Moses and when Moses met the sorcerers; the author rejects this anachronistic reading because the cited passages were revealed much later.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالضحى، لأنها الساعة التي كلم فيها موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النيسابوري والرازي
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi and al-Razi liken the duha hour to the whole night, just as Muhammad is said to equal all prophets and their communities.
rows.anchor: توازي جميع الليل، كما أن محمداً - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يوازي جميع الأنبياء وأممهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author excludes esoteric readings that turn duha and night into the Prophet's face and hair, male and female relatives, knowledge and forgiveness, or Islam's rise and later estrangement.
rows.anchor: ولا نقف بعد هذا عند تأويلات الإشاريين بأن الضحى وجه محمد، - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والليل شعره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read wadda'aka with a doubled dāl, while some read the verb with a light dāl; eloquent Arabic generally avoided the simple triliteral form.
rows.anchor: والقراءة بالدال المشددة هي قراءة الجمهور، وقرأ بعضهم:

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari cites poetry using wada'a, while al-Jawhari says such usage may be confined to poetic necessity; Khifaf uses mawdu' to mean left.
rows.anchor: ولكن الجوهري في (الصحاح) صرح بأن مثل هذا ربما جاء

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says eloquent Arabic dispensed with the simple triliteral form, and a lexicon commentator's objection does not undo that point.
rows.anchor: لا تدفع ما قاله: أبو حيان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Wada' means leaving, with tawdi' intensifying the sense because a person who bids farewell leaves you emphatically.
rows.anchor: وقال الومخشري: "التوديع مبالغة في الدةع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root occurs elsewhere in Qur'anic imperative and mustawda' forms, while 93:3 is its only past-tense verb use.
rows.anchor: ولم يجيء من المادة في القرآن، بصيغة الفعل الماضي إلا آية الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qala means intense hatred; its sensory root may suggest agitation, which extends to withdrawal and departure, and Ibn Sida defines it as utmost hatred followed by leaving.
rows.anchor: قليته قلى أبغضته وكرهته غاية الكره فتركته

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib glosses qala in both Qur'anic occurrences as intense hatred and aversion.
rows.anchor: وبشدة البغض، فسرها "الراغب" في (المفردات)

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the omitted object of qala is obvious and shortened, comparing the omission to another Qur'anic construction.
rows.anchor: إنه اختصار لفظي، لظهور المحذوف

rows.speaker: الطبري وأبو حيان
rows.claim: Al-Tabari and Abu Hayyan explain the omitted addressee through the preceding mention of the Prophet and as concise expression.
rows.anchor: إنه اكتفاء بفهم السامع لمعناه، إذ كان قد تقدم ذلك قوله: ما ودعك

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi adds that omission preserves the rhyme endings of the surah.
rows.anchor: وهو رعاية الفاصلة: والضحى سجى

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi gives three reasons: the earlier kaaf suffices, rhyme requires omission, or the unrestricted object includes all who love the Prophet; the author rejects the expansive reading as unsupported by context.
rows.anchor: فائدة الإطلاق، أي أنه ما قلاك ولا أحداً من أصحابك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects rhyme alone as the reason for omission: the Qur'anic style is not governed by form alone, and the surah's last verse does not follow a th-rhyme or use a substitute verb to force one.
rows.anchor: ليس من المقبول عندنا أن يقوم البيان القرآني على اعتبار لفظي محض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressee is clear from what precedes; omitting the harsh verb comforts the Prophet, since qala implies expulsion and severe hatred, while tawdi' can suggest reluctant parting and hoped-for return.
rows.anchor: تحاشي خطابه تعالى لحبيبه المصطفى في مقام الإيناس: ما قلاك

rows.speaker: الرازي والنيسابوري
rows.claim: Some explain the delay by the Prophet's failure to say God willing after promising answers to Jewish questions, or by a puppy or untrimmed nails preventing Gabriel's entry; the author rejects these as strained, and notes the puppy story conflicts with the children's post-Hijra birth.
rows.anchor: أن اليهود سألوا النبي عن ثلاث نسائل: الروح، وذي القرنين واصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the pause cannot mean removal of prophethood; at most it signaled death, which would be good for the Prophet because of his afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: أن إنقطاع الوحي لا يجوز أن يكون لعزل عن النبوة، بل أقصى ما في هذا الباب أنه أمارة الموت

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says that the Prophet's receipt of the verse's honor was followed by assurance of still greater honor in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: كالرازي الذي ذكر فيها وجوهاً ثلاثة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi labels as his own speculation that the Prophet's future conditions would be better than his past ones, then lists reasons involving divine pleasure, his community, witness, and lasting afterlife gifts.
rows.anchor: وقد صدره الرازي بقوله: وهو ما يخطر ببالي - وللأحوال الآتية خير لك من الماضية

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh reads al-akhira and al-ula as the end and beginning of the Prophet's mission: renewed revelation would complete the religion and God's blessing.
rows.anchor: ولنهاية أمرك خير لك من بدايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although al-akhira usually means the afterlife in the Qur'an, contextual evidence can give it another sense, as in al-milla al-akhira.
rows.anchor: يغلب أنها للدار أو الحياة الآخرة، مقابلة للدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired Qur'anic expressions al-akhira wa-l-ula usually name the two lives; this surah applies them particularly to Muhammad's fear of abandonment and assures him that his future is better.
rows.anchor: فنرى آية الضحى تنفرد عنها بأنها خاصة بمحمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، في حالة بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 5 completes the reassurance: God did not leave the Prophet in the past, and his future is better.
rows.anchor: يتكامل بها التجلي الإلهي على المصطفى: ما تركك فيما مضى، وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised gift is deliberately left unrestricted; the Prophet needs only the gift that satisfies him, and commentators should not define it by their own preferences.
rows.anchor: فحسب الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الإعطاء الذي يرضيه، وليس وراء الرضى مطمح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Ibn Abbas that the promised gift is a palace in Paradise with spouses and servants; later exegetes add material details, which the author declines to impose.
rows.anchor: إنه ألفقصر في الجنة، في كل قصر ما ينبغي من الأزواج والخدم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A report treats al-Sharh and al-Duha as one surah because both recount divine favors, including sheltering the orphan and expanding the Prophet's breast.
rows.anchor: واقترنت بها في رواية تقول إن الضحى والشرح سورة واحدة لما يبدو من المناسبة

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi calls the one-surah report weak: the Qur'an as a whole is one discourse, and the change from third-person to first-person address marks separation rather than connection.
rows.anchor: وفيه ضعف، لأن القرآن كله في حكم كلام واحد

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh says most hold the surah Meccan, while some see it as a continuation of al-Duha whose promised return of revelation grounds the favor of expanded breast.
rows.anchor: السورة مكية عند الجمهور، بل زعم بعضهمأنها تتمة لسورة الضحى

rows.speaker: البقاعي
rows.claim: Al-Biqa'i calls the surah Medinan because its account of expansion and later favors seems to presuppose Muslim strength and victory; the author replies that Meccan surahs also affirm this.
rows.anchor: وقد قال "البقاعى" إنها مدنية بناء على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that al-Tabari, al-Zamakhshari, and al-Qurtubi do not discuss joining the surahs, and that exegetes use either Alam Nashrah or al-Inshirah as the title.
rows.anchor: وجاءت السورة في بعض التفاسير مثل الطبري باسم "ألم نشرح"

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari understands expanding the breast as opening it to guidance, faith, knowledge of God, and truth, making it a vessel for wisdom.
rows.anchor: إنه الشرح للهدى والإيمان بالله ومعرفة الحق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says expansion makes room for prophetic burdens and persecution, or for knowledge and wisdom, removing the constraints of ignorance.
rows.anchor: وقال الومخشري: "شرحنا لك صدرك، فسحناه حتى وسع هموم النبوة

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh says God expanded the Prophet's breast by freeing him from confusion and distress at his people's stubborn opposition.
rows.anchor: بإخراجه من تلك الحيرة التي كان يضيق لها صدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author accepts these related spiritual readings as plausible explanations of expansion.
rows.anchor: وهي معان متقاربة ومقبولة

rows.speaker: النيسابوري وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi and a report from Ibn Abbas allow literal chest expansion, with Gabriel opening the Prophet's chest, washing the heart, and filling it with knowledge and faith; the author says this should be tested against Qur'anic usage.
rows.anchor: لما يروى من أن جبرائيل أتاه وشق صدره وأخرج قلبه وغسله

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib connects this verse with Moses' prayer and the description of one whose breast God expands for Islam, concluding that expansion is divine light, calm, and spirit.
rows.anchor: شرح الصدر بسطه بنور إلهي وسكينة من جهة الله وروح منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verses concern Moses' mission and believers opened to Islam's light, so they support a spiritual sense rather than cutting open and cleansing a physical heart.
rows.anchor: ولا مجال لقول بشق الصدر وانتزاع القلب ثم غسله وتطهيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Qur'anic uses include a breast opened to disbelief and a breast opened to Islam or constricted in error, placing the phrase in a moral and spiritual pattern.
rows.anchor: وفي القرآن الكريم من آيات شرح الصدر. غي ما ذكره الراغب آيتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five Meccan passages associate expansion with light and ease and contrast it with hardness, error, constriction, and disbelief, reinforcing a spiritual reading.
rows.anchor: والآيات الخمس مكية. والشرح فيها جميعاً للصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across Qur'anic examples, expanding the breast means faith, truth's light, certainty, and peace, not a physical operation.
rows.anchor: وهذا التتبع، يزيدنا بعداً عن المعنى المادي لشرح الصجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular sadr in the Qur'an appears with expansion or with distress, tightness, and constraint, referring to inner states in addresses to Muhammad and Moses.
rows.anchor: إما مع الشرح في الآيات الخمس التي أشرنا إليها، وإما مع الضيق والحرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These Qur'anic patterns make it difficult to read the Prophet's breast literally as the bodily organ or as an inventory of appetite, desire, and anger.
rows.anchor: يجعلنا نتردد في تفسير الصدر هنا بالجارحة كما ذهب النيسابورى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic plural sudur carry healing, satanic whispering, spite, reluctance, and fear, all inward conditions rather than a physical chest-opening event.
rows.anchor: أو وسوسة الشيطان في آية الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects exegetical additions of knowledge and wisdom from a physical opening because the Qur'anic contexts do not support them.
rows.anchor: ولا مجال معه، لتزيد لا يحتمله صريح السياق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the question as a denial that in effect asserts expansion, paraphrasing it as We expanded your breast and removed your burden.
rows.anchor: إنه استفهم عن انتقاء الشرح على وجه الإنكار، فأفاد إثبات الشرح وإيجابه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: If the question must be classified, Abu Hayyan says it is confirmatory rather than negative; the author rejects al-Zamakhshari's paraphrase as far from the verse's exact form.
rows.anchor: فهو على وجه التقرير كما قال أبو حيان، لا الإنكار كما ذهب الزمخشري

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some say the first-person plural in sharah magnifies the act or indicates Gabriel's mediation.
rows.anchor: فائدة العدول من المتكلم إلى الجمع، إما تعظيم حال الشرح، وإما الإعلام بتوسط الملك جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dhikr gains majesty from its association with God and from its established use for revelation; God's raising Muhammad's mention thus gives the fullest reassurance and honor.
rows.anchor: وهذا مما يضفى على كلمة الذكر جلالاً ورفعه، لكبرة ما تفترن بذات الجلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author declines to specify exactly how the Prophet's mention was raised: being chosen as messenger already exceeds every worldly ambition for an orphan from a poor family.
rows.anchor: فحسب محمد أن اصطفاه الله رسولاً، ليكون له من هذا الاصطفاء ما يجاوز كل مطمح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa links ease causally to the prior gifts of expanded breast, removed burden, and raised mention; inna and repetition reinforce reassurance and remove doubt.
rows.anchor: في الفاء هنا، مع معنى الترتيب دلالة السببية، فهي تقرر مل يترتب على ما سبق بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repetition in short surahs need not be rhetorical excess when the occasion calls for reinforcing assurance.
rows.anchor: حيث لا مجال في مثلها لقول بالإطناب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says ma'a makes relief follow hardship soon, so that the coming ease is treated as if accompanying it for comfort.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: "إن "مع" للصحبة

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi likewise says nearness makes the time of ease seem continuous with hardship and strengthens hope.
rows.anchor: جعل الزمان القريب كالمتصل والمقارن زيادة في التسلية وقوة الرجاء

rows.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh says ma'a secures hope that relief must come, as though already with hardship.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالمعية لتوثيق الأمل بأنه لابد منه، كأنه معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author agrees that ma'a signals accompaniment but rejects the simile and the generalization to believers: the context chiefly reassures the Prophet, and the ease is joined to hardship.
rows.anchor: والأولى إسقاط كاف التشبيه، وفهم الآيتين على أن اليسر مقترن بالعسر

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: They argue that repeated definite al-usr refers to one known hardship, while the indefinite yusr presents two distinct eases; a report from the Prophet says one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: فسره الفراء والزجاج: "العسر مذكور بالألف واللام

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Al-Bahr reports the view that one hardship comes with two eases because hardship is definite and ease indefinite.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مع كل عسر يسران، من حيث إن العسر معرف بالعهد

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani warns that repeating a sentence about a horse with a sword does not prove the horse has two swords.
rows.anchor: من المعلوم أن القائل إذا قال إن مع الفارس سيفاً إن مع الفارس سيفاً

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi explores generic or definite hardship and repeated or new sentences, concluding that a sound hadith would require one hardship and two distinct eases; without it, several readings remain possible.
rows.anchor: وتوسع النيسابورى في افتراض إحتمالات شتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the competing grammatical scenarios needlessly complex; some commentators also identify the two eases as worldly and afterlife relief or as conquests and afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: والذي في جمهرة التفاسير لا يكاد يخرج عن هذه الإحتمالات والإفتراضات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second verse confirms the first to strengthen the Prophet's inward certainty in God's gifts, rather than introduce a separate promise.
rows.anchor: والذي نطمئن إليه، هو أن الآية الثانية تأكيد للأولى، لتقوية اليقين النفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-usr is definite by reference to the Prophet's distress at facing entrenched idolatry, while indefinite yusr leaves the relief open rather than setting limits on it.
rows.anchor: والراجح أن "ال" في العسر، للعهد لا للاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Usr denotes the most severe hardship and struggle, with Arabic usage for intense physical constriction and Qur'anic descriptions of the Day's hardship and other acute trials.
rows.anchor: والعسر أشد المشقة والمكابدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusr is the opposite of hardship; Arabic also uses it for wealth and for something prepared or achieved without difficulty, conveying relief and release here.
rows.anchor: وكثيراً ما يأتي اليسر في القرآن نقيضاً للعسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faragh literally means becoming empty after fullness, whether of a vessel or of the mind; Qur'anic examples use it both physically and figuratively.
rows.anchor: الفراغ في اللغة هو الخلو بعد امتلاء. يكون مادياً حسياً مثل: فرغ الإناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The late Meccan surah is commonly placed eighty-first in revelation order, after al-Naba'; its opening oath omits the subject before five successive descriptions, inviting many interpretations.
rows.anchor: السورة مكية متأخرة، فهي الواحدة والثمانون على المشهور في ترتيب النزول نزلت بعد النبأ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One reported view identifies the nazi'at as angels pulling human souls; it is attributed to Ibn Abbas and another named authority in the source.
rows.anchor: أنها الملائكة تنزع نفوس بني آدم - عم عبد الله وإبن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Another view identifies the nazi'at as stars moving from one horizon to another.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي النجوم تنزع من أفق إلى أفق - عن الحسن وقتادة وأبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says they are souls yearning for their homes and inclinations.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي النفوس تحن إلى أوطانها وتنزع إلى مذاهبها - عن السدي

rows.speaker: عطاء وعكرمة
rows.claim: A reported view identifies them as bows drawing arrows.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي القسى تنزع بالسهام - عن عطاء وعكرمة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A further report from Ata identifies them as groups drawing bows.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي الجماعات النازعات بالقسى - عن عطاء أيضاً

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they are deaths pulling souls away.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي المنايا تنزع النفوس - عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam records that they are wild animals heading toward pasture.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي الوحش تنزع إلى الكلأ - حكاه يحي بن سلام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's Kashshaf gives the view that they are horses of raiders pulling at their reins.
rows.anchor: هي خيل الغزاة تنزع في أعنتها - جاء في الكشاف

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib's al-Mufradat includes the view that they are winds uprooting people through their force.
rows.anchor: هي الريح تقلع القوم لشدة هبوبها - جاء في المفردات

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari selects three principal readings: angels, stars, or raiding horses; al-Raghib selects angels or wind.
rows.anchor: وأشهر هذه الأقوال جميعاً، أنها الملائكة تنزع أرواح بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with al-Duha and al-Adiyat, the author reads the opening wāw as directing attention to sensory, observable realities that prepare for an unseen matter; he says the approach suits several other Meccan oath surahs.
rows.anchor: القرآن يعدل في هذا الأسلوب عن الأصل اللغوي للتعظيم بالقسم إلى استعمال بلاغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects angels as the referent because their work is not sensory evidence, and skeptics who believed in such angels would already accept resurrection.
rows.anchor: ليست الملائكة في نزعها للأرواح، وسبقها إلى تدبير أمر الله، مما يدخل في نطاق الحسيات المدركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers horses charging without specifying raiders: Meccan Muslims had no raiding horses or political domains, and the passage needs an observed event rather than a later post-Hijra projection.
rows.anchor: فما كان للمسلمين في العهد المكي خيل تغزو، ولا كان هناك دار سلام ودار حرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charging horses recall al-Adiyat, where their raid prepares the audience to imagine resurrection, graves emptied and inner secrets exposed.
rows.anchor: وقد لفت القرآن في (سورة العاديات) إلى الخيل عاديات ضبحاً

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib identifies al-tamma al-kubra as the Resurrection; Ibn Abbas says it is the second trumpet blast, while Mujahid says it is when the two groups are driven toward their destinations.
rows.anchor: وهي النفخة الثانية فيما روي عن "ابن عباس" أو وقت سوق أهل الجنة إليها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari lists all three interpretations and appears to prefer the Resurrection; the word occurs nowhere else in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وجاء الزمخشري في الكشاف بهذه الأقوال الثلاثة متتالية

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib derives tamma from an overflowing sea; Arabic also uses al-tamma for an overwhelming calamity, which supports al-Zamakhshari's interpretation as Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وأخذها "الراغب" من الطم أي البحر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes remembering as recalling after forgetting and compares the Day when God reports people's deeds, which they had forgotten.
rows.anchor: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعاً فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers a relative reading of ma: the things or deeds the person strove for.
rows.anchor: وقد أختار أبو حيان الموصولة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows ma to be either a relative pronoun or a verbal noun, without choosing between them.
rows.anchor: أما الزمخشري، فقال بهما معاً، دون ترجيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the verbal-noun reading as broader: the human will remember his striving, echoing the statement that each person has only what he strove for.
rows.anchor: والذي نراه أن المصدرة أعم وأولى بالمقام، فيكون المعنى: يوم يتذكر الإنسان مسعاه
